Package com.sc.demo.sse.examples.basic

Class EventController

java.lang.Object
com.sc.demo.sse.examples.basic.EventController
@RestController @RequestMapping("/api") @CrossOrigin(origins={"http://localhost:5500","http://127.0.0.1:5500"}) public class EventController extends Object
Exposes the server-sent events stream.

Each GET /api/stream request creates an independent stream that sends ten JSON notifications, two seconds apart, before completing. Events use the name notification and have incrementing IDs for clients to inspect. This example does not retain events or replay them based on Last-Event-ID; reconnecting clients start a new stream.

SSE is a unidirectional protocol over a long-lived HTTP response. A browser can consume this endpoint with the native EventSource API, which handles reconnection at the transport level.

  • Method Details

    • stream

      @GetMapping(value="/stream", produces="text/event-stream") public org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.method.annotation.SseEmitter stream()
      Opens a stream and sends a finite sequence of notifications.

      The response has the text/event-stream media type. Each event has a unique-in-this-stream ID, the notification event name, and a JSON-serialized EventController.Notification payload. The emitter times out after 60 seconds. The scheduled task is cancelled when the client disconnects, the stream completes, or the emitter times out.

      Returns:
      the asynchronous SSE response
